hindi: मेद यानी चर्बी का सार अस्थि, स्नायु यानी हड्डियों को बाँधने वाले तन्तु और सन्धियाँ हैं; किट्ट यानी अपशिष्ट पसीना है।
english: Of fat (medas), the essence (sāra) is bone (asthi), ligaments (snāyu) and joints (sandhi); the waste (kiṭṭa) is sweat.
notes: Copula understood. asthi-snāyu-sandhayaḥ is read as one dvandva list of three items (bone, ligaments, joints), all given as the essence as printed; the alternative 'joints of bone and ligament' is possible. The pattern essence (sāra) / waste (kiṭṭa or mala) for each dhātu continues from units 121-123 (chunk 3).

words.gloss: hair of the head (keśa); body hair (loman)

hindi: अस्थि का सार मज्जा यानी हड्डी के भीतर का गूदा है; किट्ट यानी अपशिष्ट केश, रोम यानी शरीर के बाल और नख हैं।
english: Of bone (asthi), the essence is marrow (majjā); the waste (kiṭṭa) is the hair of the head, the body hair (loman) and the nails.

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction (majjā ends in a long vowel, kiṭṭam begins with k); read as two words: essence = marrow, waste = hair etc.

notes: Copula understood. 'majjākiṭṭaṃ' is split into two words because the sense (essence, then waste) requires it and the neighbouring units follow this pattern; a compound 'marrow-waste' does not fit. majjā = marrow in this anatomy unit.

hindi: मज्जा का तो सार शुक्र यानी वीर्य है; मल यानी अपशिष्ट आँख का मल और त्वचाओं का स्नेह यानी तेल या वसा है।
english: Of marrow (majjan), however, the essence is śukra (semen); the waste (mala) is the excrement of the eye (akṣi-viṭ) and the oiliness (sneha) of the skins.
notes: Copula understood. 'tvacām' = of the skins (plural, as elsewhere in this chapter). The two items after mala (eye-excrement, oiliness of the skins) are read as the waste; the Sanskrit has no 'and'. majjan = marrow here (anatomy unit).

hindi: शुक्र यानी वीर्य का सार ओजस् यानी जीवन-सार है।
english: Of śukra (semen), the essence is ojas (vital essence).
notes: Copula understood. 'sāram' is neuter here, whereas the neighbouring units have masculine 'sāraḥ' (sāra takes both genders); read as nominative neuter, or as an accusative with a verb understood; the sense is the same. Not corrected.

words.gram: karmadhāraya + abstract suffix, f. inst. sg.

hindi: और अत्यन्त शुद्धता के कारण इसमें मल यानी अपशिष्ट का अभाव है।
english: And through extreme purity there is absence of waste (mala) in this.
notes: Copula supplied in the translation ('there is'), as the noun 'abhāva' needs it. 'asmin' (in this) is not tied to a noun in the unit; it is read as the śukra/ojas of unit 127 and is left as 'this'.

hindi: दूसरे लोग तो इसी कारण उसका पाक यानी पकना स्वीकार नहीं करते।
english: Others, however, for this very reason do not accept a cooking (pāka) of it.

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between anye and punar (the following punar ata eva is regular sandhi)

notes: 'tasya' (of it) is left as a plain pronoun; it is read as referring to the essence of śukra (unit 127-128). Literally icchanti = 'wish, want'; 'accept' is the natural sense. 'ata eva' = ataḥ eva (regular).

hindi: दूसरे लोग तो शुक्र यानी वीर्य के सार को ही गर्भ यानी भ्रूण मानते हैं।
english: Others, however, hold the essence of śukra (semen) to be the garbha (embryo) itself.
notes: Two accusatives with āmananti: the essence of śukra and the garbha, read as 'hold X to be Y'. The alternative 'they declare the garbha, the essence of śukra, itself' gives the same sense. garbha = embryo (standard).

words.gram: dvandva + abstract suffix, f. inst. sg.

words.gloss: slight (īṣat); sound (śabda); abundant (pracura); sense of the compound uncertain

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: वायु तो अग्नि और आहार की अधिकता और अल्पता से, उस-उस विशेष मूर्च्छना यानी सम्भवतः सघन या प्रबल होने से, अमूर्त, शब्द वाला, थोड़े शब्द में प्रचुर, अथवा अल्प, पञ्चात्मा यानी पाँच स्वरूप वाला होकर कोष्ठ यानी पेट के भीतरी भाग में प्रकट होता है।
english: On a conjectural reading: Wind (vāyu), however, through the abundance and scarcity of the fire (agni) and of the food, from this-and-that particular mūrcchanā (probably intensification), appears in the koṣṭha (storehouse, belly cavity), bodiless (amūrta), sound-possessing, abundant in slight sound, or small, and five-natured (pañcātmā).

text_flags.why: possible: 'ātamā' is not a word; pañcātmā ('five-natured', the wind with five forms) fits the sense and differs by one stray letter

words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between the two tasmāt (t before t is unchanged); the following t+m→n, d+a are regular sandhi. Also amūrttaḥ = amūrtaḥ (rtt normalisation, recorded once in the glossary)

notes: Hard sentence; confidence low. (1) 'pañcātmā' is adopted for printed 'paṃcātamā', hence the conjectural mark. (2) mūrcchanā: sense uncertain (swoon / thickening / intensification); kept as mūrcchanā with a hedged gloss. (3) 'īṣacchabdapracuro'lpo vā': read as three descriptors of the wind, 'īṣat-śabda-pracura' (abundant in slight sound; literal) and 'alpa' (small) joined by vā; it may instead mean 'with slight or abundant sound, or small'. (4) bahvalpatayā is a dvandva: 'abundance and scarcity' (literal), natural sense 'according to how much or how little'. (5) The five forms (pañcātmā) are not named here.

hindi: और ऐसा करके देह में सभी भाव यानी पदार्थ या अवस्थाएँ अन्न से बने हुए ही हैं।
english: And having thus done, all states (bhāva) in the body are made of food alone.
notes: 'evaṃ kṛtvā' is rendered literally; the idiom is probably 'this being so'. Copula understood. 'annamayā' is annamayāḥ with the visarga lost before eva (regular -āḥ + vowel).

hindi: उसी से यह शरीर-यन्त्र इस प्रकार देर तक, भीतर और बाहर न्यास यानी धरोहर के रूप में, अटूट प्रवाह के साथ, स्वास्थ्य, बल और वृद्धि से युक्त होकर, जब तक कर्म का उपादान यानी ग्रहण है तब तक चलाया जाता है।
english: By that alone, this body-machine (śarīra-yantra), thus, for a long time, as a deposit (nyāsa) within and without, with an unbroken flow, endowed with health, strength and growth, is kept going for as long as the taking up (upādāna) of action (karma).

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between antar and bahiḥ (r before b is unchanged)
words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between yuktam and yāvat, and between yāvat and karma (t before k is unchanged)

notes: Confidence low. 'nyāsam antarbahiḥ' is not clearly construed: nyāsa (deposit, placing) is taken as an adverbial 'as a deposit' and 'within and without' goes with it; other readings (e.g. 'placed within and without') are possible. 'yāvat karmopādānam' is read as 'for as long as the taking up of karma (action)', i.e. as long as karma is taken up; it may mean 'as far as karma takes it'. The subject (this body-machine) is in the nominative/accusative form śarīra-yantram. 'tena' is left as 'by that' (the food of the preceding units).

words.gloss: food (anna); rasa; throwing up (utkṣepa); and the like (ādi); bound (baddha); channel (srotas)

hindi: परन्तु अन्यथा, या तो अन्न-रस के उत्क्षेप यानी ऊपर फेंके जाने आदि से बँधे हुए स्रोतस् के कारण, धातुओं के उस प्रवाह के बीच जो ठीक से जुड़ा हुआ नहीं है, कट जाता है, या रोग का पात्र बन जाता है।
english: But otherwise, either, with the srotas (channels) bound by the throwing up (utkṣepa) of food-rasa and the like, it is cut off in the midst of the flow of the dhātus, which is not duly joined, or it becomes a vessel (bhājana) of disease (vyādhi).
notes: Confidence low. The subject is not stated (the body-machine of unit 133 is understood; the English 'it' is a bare pronoun for the verb, no noun added). 'vā ... vā' is read as 'either ... or'. 'baddhasrotasā' (instrumental singular) is read with the unstated subject; it may instead be 'srotasāṃ' (genitive plural, 'of the srotas bound by ...'). 'antarā' with the accusative 'pravāham' = 'in the midst of the flow'. utkṣepa = throwing up, ejection.

hindi: परन्तु दूसरे लोग वर्णन करते हैं।
english: But others describe.
notes: GROUPING: the unit is a lead-in; the description follows in unit 136 (appears to continue there). The object of 'varṇayanti' is not stated and not supplied.

words.gloss: throat (kaṇṭha); tube (nāḍī; probably the gullet); rush, leap (pluti)
great (mahā); hollow (nimna; probably the abdominal cavity)
licked over, touched (conjecture for printed blīḍhaḥ)
rasa; trace, small portion (leśa) (conjecture for printed rasleśo)
production (abhinirvṛtti) (conjecture for printed abhinirvatti); immediately after (samanantaram)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: निगले जाते ही आहार की कण्ठनाड़ी यानी सम्भवतः अन्ननलिका से होकर प्लुति यानी तेज़ बहाव होता है; उसके महानिम्न यानी सम्भवतः उदर-गुहा में उतर जाने पर जो-जो अंश कायाग्नि यानी शरीर की अग्नि से चाटा गया है, वह पाक को पहुँचाया जाता है; उस-उस अंश का ही प्रसाद नामक रस का लेश, उत्पन्न होने के तुरन्त बाद, सभी धातुओं में समान रूप से, बन्द और खुले से, द्वारों द्वारा, खुले मुख वाले अस्पष्ट शब्द वाले स्रोतसों में फैलकर, अधिक भाग पहले जाता है और बारी-बारी से अन्य में भी अनुसरण करता है।
english: On a conjectural reading: Of food, just as it is swallowed, there is the rush (pluti) through the throat-tube (kaṇṭha-nāḍī, probably the gullet); of that, having descended into the great hollow (mahānimna, probably the abdominal cavity), whichever part is licked over by the bodily fire (kāyāgni) is brought to cooking; of each such part, a trace of rasa called prasāda (clear essence), immediately upon its production, spread equally into all the dhātus by the enclosed and open (ones), through the doors, into the srotas with open mouths (unclear word); the greater (part) goes first, and by turns follows in the others also.

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between āhārasya and kaṃṭha-
the final m is printed on the next token ('mavatīrṇasya'); a misplaced space
the initial m belongs to the preceding mahānimna (mahānimnam avatīrṇasya); misplaced space
possible: 'blīḍha' is not a word; avalīḍha (licked over, touched) fits (b/v interchange in this print, vowel dropped); ālīḍha is an alternative
possible: rasleśo has lost its a (rasa-leśaḥ); abhinirvatti has lost its ṛ (abhinirvṛtti); also rtt/tt spelling
possible: doubled s; pravisṛta (spread out)
damaged: 'akāsanneṣu' is not a word; possibly 'āsanneṣu' (near) with a stray ka; left unsplit as unclear
words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between bhūyān and prathamataṃ; and printed final ṃ for ḥ (possible)
possible: 'paryāyaiṇa' is not a form; paryāyeṇa (instrumental, 'by turns') + itareṣu + api

notes: Confidence low; heavily damaged. Conjectures adopted in `words` (hence the conjectural mark in both translations): avalīḍhaḥ, rasa-leśaḥ, abhinirvṛtti, pravisṛtaḥ, prathamataḥ, paryāyeṇa. Left unclear: 'akāsanneṣu' (guess in the flag only). The construction after 'pravisṛtaḥ' is uncertain: 'saṃvṛtāsaṃvṛtaiḥ' (by the enclosed and open ones) and 'dvāraiḥ' (by the doors) are both instrumental; 'vivṛtamukheṣu ... srotaḥsu' = in the srotas with open mouths. 'plutiḥ' is rendered 'rush' (leap, passage). 'mahānimna' = great hollow, probably the stomach/belly cavity (hedged). 'kaṇṭhanāḍī' = throat-tube, probably the gullet. 'bhūyān' (the greater) is read as the greater part of that rasa-trace. GROUPING: appears to continue the description introduced in unit 135 ('others describe').

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: इस प्रकार अन्न-रस ही सीधे सभी धातुओं का, केवल किसी काल-भेद से, पोषण करता है।
english: On a conjectural reading: Thus the food-rasa itself directly nourishes all the dhātus, by only some difference of time.

text_flags.why: possible: printed 'antarasa' = anta-rasa; anna-rasa (food-rasa) fits (ta/na confusion, seen elsewhere in this book) and matches āhāra-rasa in unit 119; 'rasa eva' is regular hiatus
words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction (t before s is unchanged)

notes: 'anna-rasa' is a conjecture for printed 'antarasa'; the printed form read as anta-rasa ('end rasa') or antara-rasa ('inner rasa') does not suit as well. 'kenacid eva kālabhedena' = by just some difference of time (literal).

words.gram: tat-puruṣa + abstract suffix, f. acc. sg.

hindi: परन्तु धातु अपने स्वरूप के नाश से दूसरी धातु की अवस्था को प्राप्त नहीं होते।
english: But the dhātus do not pass into the state of another dhātu through the crushing (upamarda) of their own form.
notes: 'iti' marks the end of the statement (the view of 'others', units 135-138; appears to be the end of that view) and is not translated. 'pratipadyanta iti' = pratipadyante + iti (regular, printed 'taiti').

hindi: अग्नि यानी पाचन-अग्नि तो बल के भेद से चार प्रकार की होती है: सम यानी समान, विषम यानी असमान, तीक्ष्ण यानी तेज़ और मन्द यानी धीमी।
english: Agni (digestive fire), however, is of four kinds by difference of strength: sama (even), viṣama (uneven), tīkṣṇa (sharp) and manda (slow).

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between balabhedena and caturvidhaḥ

notes: agni = digestive fire (the sense in this passage). The four names are kept with plain glosses.

hindi: उनमें सम वह है जो ठीक से ही खाए गए अन्न को ठीक से पचाती है।
english: Among these, the sama (even) one is that which properly digests food that has been properly taken.
notes: Copula understood. The subject (agni) is carried from unit 139. Tokens 'samyagevopayuktamannaṃ' = samyak eva upayuktam annam (regular sandhi).

hindi: विषम अग्नि अनुचित रीति से खाए हुए को भी पचा लेती है और ठीक से खाए हुए को भी नहीं पचाती।
english: The viṣama (uneven) one digests even what is improperly taken, and even when properly (taken) does not digest.

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction between api and ca

notes: The object is not stated (annam of unit 140 understood); no noun supplied.

hindi: तीक्ष्ण अग्नि अनुचित रीति से खाए हुए को भी शीघ्र पचा देती है; वही बढ़ती हुई अत्यग्नि यानी अत्यधिक अग्नि हो जाती है।
english: The tīkṣṇa (sharp) one digests quickly even what is improperly taken; that very one, increasing, becomes atyagni (excessive fire).
notes: atyagni (ati-agni) is kept as a term with the plain gloss 'excessive fire'; the text does not describe it further here.

words.gloss: belly (udara); heaviness (gaurava); flatulent distension (ādhmāna); constipation (vibandha); gurgling (āṭopa); intestinal murmuring (āntra-kūjana); dryness (śoṣa) of the mouth (mukha); stiffness (stambha) of the anus (pāyu); and the like (ādi)

hindi: मन्द तो ठीक से भी खाए हुए को उदर का भारीपन, आध्मान यानी पेट फूलना, विबन्ध यानी मल का रुकना, आटोप यानी गड़गड़ाहट, आन्त्र-कूजन यानी आँतों की आवाज़, मुख का सूखना, पायु यानी गुदा की जकड़न आदि आम यानी अपक्व कच्चे के लक्षण दिखाकर देर से पचाती है।
english: The manda (slow) one, even what is properly taken, after showing the signs of āma (raw, undigested material) — heaviness of the belly, flatulent distension (ādhmāna), constipation (vibandha), gurgling (āṭopa), intestinal murmuring (āntra-kūjana), dryness of the mouth, stiffness of the anus (pāyu) and the like — digests after a long time.

text_flags.why: words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction (t before p is unchanged)

notes: The long compound is read as one dvandva of seven items followed by 'ādi' (and the like); 'udara-gaurava' is taken as 'heaviness of the belly' (udara = belly, not the disease), though 'udara' and 'gaurava' could be two items. āma = raw, undigested stuff (standard); the exact items are as printed. ādhmāna is neuter.

words.gloss: how much more, what to say of

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर: ज्वाला और अंगारे वाली बाहरी अग्नि से भी पाक सदा एक ही रूप का नहीं होता; तो भीतर आश्रित ऊष्मा से, सम होने पर भी, कहना ही क्या; इसलिए उसकी प्रयत्न से रक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: On a conjectural reading: Even with external fire consisting of flame and embers, cooking is not always of one form; what to say, then, of the heat lodged within, even when it is even (sama)! Therefore one should protect it with effort.

text_flags.why: possible: 'oṣmamanā' is not a form; ūṣmaṇā (by heat) fits, with a doubled syllable (ma) in print; the agni of the preceding units is the heat meant
words not separated in print; no sandhi applies at the junction (t before t is unchanged)

notes: ūṣmaṇā is a conjecture adopted in `words` (hence the conjectural mark). 'tam' (it) is a stated pronoun, taken as the agni. 'kimuta' is read as a rhetorical 'how much more / what to say of'. 'samena' agrees with ūṣman (even, steady). 'pākobhavati' = pākaḥ bhavati (regular sandhi).

words.gloss: doṣa; treatment (upakramaṇīya, probably a section or chapter title); stated (ukta)
Vāta; and the like (ādi); remedy, means (sādhana)
grahaṇī (probably a digestive disorder); disease (roga); prescribed (vihita)

hindi: वहाँ श्रेष्ठ सात्म्य यानी अनुकूल के साथ समान रूप से, अपने-अपने अनुसार निम्न के द्वारा अन्य को क्रमशः समता तक पहुँचाकर, श्रेष्ठ के द्वारा रक्षा करे — दोषोपक्रमणीय में कहे वात आदि के साधन से और ग्रहणी रोग यानी सम्भवतः पाचन के विकार में बताए औषध और व्यायाम के योगों से।
english: Therein, equally with the best sātmya (what suits), each according to its own, having brought the others gradually to equality by means of the lesser (avara), one should protect (it) with the best (pravara), by the remedy for Vāta and the like stated in the doṣa-treatment section (doṣopakramaṇīya, probably a chapter title), and by the combinations of medicines and exercises prescribed in grahaṇī disease (grahaṇī-roga, probably a digestive disorder).
notes: Confidence low: the sentence is elliptical. 'pravareṇa sātmyena samam', 'avareṇa itarān' and the second 'pravareṇa' are all instrumentals whose exact roles (sātmya of food and conduct? the stronger and weaker agnis?) are not stated; the translation keeps them literal. 'samam' is read as 'equally' (alternatives: 'together with'). 'doṣopakramaṇīya' is read as a reference to a section on doṣa treatment (probably a chapter title elsewhere in the work; not verified). Closing 'iti' marks the end of the statement. 'it' in 'protect (it)' is the agni, not stated.

hindi: और इस विषय में यह है:
english: And on this matter there is:
notes: Lead-in formula; the verses that follow (units 147 onward) are its content. The verses that follow (unit 147 onward) appear to be its content; no break is asserted.

hindi: अपने धातु के समान रंग वाले, गोल, मोटे और बारीक।
english: Equal in colour to their own dhātu, round, thick and fine (ones).
